profiles.name: Leroy4522
profiles.tagline: APPROACH SHANKS WITH A SIDE OF DRAMA
profiles.profile: This bag is a demolition derby built around a tee ball that occasionally shows up with a pulse and everything after that trying to sue for damages. The weird part is the floor is still playable enough to hang around the front, which tells you the scoring is coming from survival, not competence. He can keep a round from fully combusting, but the irons are doing that thing where they make you check whether the face is actually still attached. When the driver is merely bad instead of catastrophic, the rest of the game still finds a way to hold the whole thing together with duct tape and regret.

profiles.name: graycrum
profiles.tagline: SHORT GAME CARRYING A FULLY UNRELIABLE BAG
profiles.profile: This one is basically a short-game hustler trapped in a golf swing that keeps trying to get him arrested. The touch around the greens is real, and when the putter isn’t being weird he can absolutely drag a round into respectable territory even while the long game is acting like it got lost on the way to the course. The problem is the ceiling keeps getting mugged by the irons, so the profile comes off volatile: one week he looks tidy, the next week the tee ball and approach play are setting fire to the good stuff. That’s not stability; that’s a rescue mission.

profiles.name: derekldavis
profiles.tagline: TEE BALLS THAT LEAVE THE COUNTY
profiles.profile: This is a full-contact experience off the tee, and not in the fun way. The long game keeps showing up like it owes the rest of the bag money, and the result is a steady diet of damaged holes where the margin for error is already nonexistent. There are tiny pockets of usefulness in there, but they get buried under a profile that spends most of its time bailing water with a spoon. He doesn’t just miss; he misses in a way that turns every hole into a math problem nobody asked for. The swing issues are loud, repetitive, and rude.
